update.title: OT-106.3: the poor person's own side, woven (#2160)
update.strand: open threads on completed clusters (#2160), OT-106.3 (M47)
update.researcher_instruction: "Weave all five OT-106.3 placements as proposed with their claims, close OT-106.3, commit and push, then read OT-05.11 (M47)." (2026-10-18)
update.method: OT-106.3 (poverty joined to the spirit or heart: Mat 5:3, Pro 16:19, Psa 109:22, with the five other S-coded M09 verses that carry an M47 word) read in their passages for OT-106's question (the researcher's three dimensions of poor/needy, #2148). Woven: Pro 13:7-8 and 2Sa 12:3-4 (10.6 Possessions), Mat 5:3-4 (Ch 6), Psa 109:22-26 (Ch 4), Psa 34:4-6 and 69:29, 33 (10.9 Waiting, and pleading). Pro 13:7: both verbs are the reflexive (hithpael) stem of 'be rich' (H6238) and 'be poor' (H7326), checked in iba.db span. Rule 77: 2-2 (Ch 6) and C-189 (Ch 4) told in touched passages; both stand; C-189 gains Psa 109:23-26 as sources.
update.claims_changed_note: Six new claims; C-189 gains sources Psa 109:23-26.

new.text: Poverty can be shown without being had: the proverb sets what a person makes himself out to be, rich or poor, against what he has
new.beyond_text: reads the reflexive verbs of Pro 13:7 as presenting oneself as rich or poor

new.text: Wealth that can ransom a life also draws threats that the poor man never hears
new.beyond_text: reads Pro 13:8's two halves as cause and contrast

new.text: In Nathan's parable the poor man's one possession is loved as kin, and it is what the rich man takes rather than his own
new.beyond_text: names the lamb 'like a daughter to him' as the poor man's attachment

new.text: Matthew 5:3 places poverty in the spirit, not in what a person has, and the next blessing is on those who mourn
new.beyond_text: reads 'poor in spirit' as poverty located inside

new.text: 'Poor and needy', said of oneself, comes with the stricken heart and the gaunt body and ends in an appeal for help
new.beyond_text: reads Psa 109:22-26 as one self-description ending in the appeal

new.text: The one who calls himself poor is the one who cries and is heard, and what he is delivered from includes his fears
new.beyond_text: joins Psa 34:4 and 34:6, and Psa 69:29 and 69:33

tellings.passage: What is had and what is shown can differ
What is had and what is shown can differ
A poor man's one possession can be loved as kin
It is lowly or proud, and it is judged
A plea can come from the poor man's own mouth
